author_or_institution: Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence
title: 2026 AI Index Report — Technical Performance
book_use: Chapters 1 and 3: large recent benchmark gains alongside benchmark-quality concerns and jagged capability; supports rapid cognitive capability improvement without treating benchmark scores as deployment reliability.

author_or_institution: Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence
title: 2026 AI Index Report — Economy
book_use: Chapters 1, 4, 5, 15 and 16: organizational AI use is widespread while agent deployment remains early; investment, capex and adoption evidence support infrastructure and distribution arguments. Use private-investment figures carefully because state-directed capital can be undercounted and surveyed adoption is not a census of deployment quality.

author_or_institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology
title: CAISI Issues Request for Information About Securing AI Agent Systems
book_use: Chapters 1, 4 and 6: authoritative description of agent systems that can plan and take autonomous actions affecting real-world systems; supports the output-to-action boundary, permission architecture and security countercase without attributing consciousness.

title: Task-Completion Time Horizons of Frontier AI Models
book_use: Chapter 6: latest public time-horizon measurements for frontier agents; evidence of longer sustained task capability on software-heavy suites while METR explicitly warns that the metric does not imply automation of all jobs or equivalent high-context professional work.

title: The Fourth Industrial Revolution: what it means and how to respond
book_use: Chapter 2: source for the popular Fourth Industrial Revolution periodization and the physical-digital-biological fusion claim; treat as framing to test rather than neutral proof.

title: What is the fourth industrial revolution?
book_use: Chapter 2: concise WEF account of the First through Fourth Industrial Revolutions, including mechanical power, electricity, digital systems, cyber-physical systems, machine intelligence and genome editing.

title: World Robotics 2025 — Global Robot Demand in Factories Doubles Over 10 Years
book_use: Chapters 3, 4 and 7: 542,000 industrial robots installed in 2024 and 4.664 million in operation; demonstrates real embodiment at scale while preserving the structured-environment limitation and geographic concentration of deployment.

title: FDA Approves First Gene Therapies to Treat Patients with Sickle Cell Disease
book_use: Chapters 3, 4, 8 and 13: Casgevy as the first FDA-approved treatment to use a novel genome-editing technology; supports the move from reading biology toward regulated therapeutic editing without implying arbitrary human redesign.

title: Infant with rare disease receives customized gene therapy
book_use: Chapters 8 and 13: first known personalized gene-editing medicine created for one patient, using CRISPR base editing for an infant with CPS1 deficiency; process from diagnosis to treatment took about six months. Preserve the single-patient nature and need for long-term follow-up.

title: Patient-Specific In Vivo Gene Editing to Treat a Rare Genetic Disease
book_use: Chapters 8 and 13: primary clinical report of customized lipid-nanoparticle-delivered base editing for severe CPS1 deficiency; supports patient-specific platform discussion while explicitly preserving short follow-up and uncertain long-term safety and efficacy.

title: Generative AI and Jobs: A 2025 Update
book_use: Chapters 3 and 11: one in four workers globally in occupations with some GenAI exposure, while most affected jobs are expected to be transformed rather than made redundant; primary counterweight to simple replacement narratives.

title: Energy and AI — Energy demand from AI
book_use: Chapters 4, 5 and 9: data-center electricity demand projected around 945 TWh in 2030 base case, just under 3% of global demand; supports the physical-infrastructure constraint beneath callable intelligence and documents longer energy-infrastructure build clocks than data centers.

title: An autonomous laboratory for the accelerated synthesis of inorganic materials
book_use: Chapter 10: A-Lab combined computation, literature-derived synthesis recipes, machine learning, active learning and robotics; realized 36 of 57 target compounds over 17 days. Use as evidence of a real closed experimental loop, not proof that autonomous science is solved.

title: Development of the autonomous lab system to support biotechnology research
book_use: Chapter 10: biotechnology autonomous-lab case integrating robotics and Bayesian optimization across culture, preprocessing, measurement, analysis and hypothesis formulation; narrow case study demonstrating closed-loop architecture rather than general scientific autonomy.

title: Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3
book_use: Chapter 10: unified deep-learning prediction across complexes containing proteins, nucleic acids, small molecules, ions and modified residues; evidence that machine prediction can change biological search while experimental validation remains necessary.

author_or_institution: Erik Brynjolfsson / Danielle Li / Lindsey R. Raymond
title: Generative AI at Work
book_use: Chapter 11: study of 5,179 customer-support agents found 14% average productivity improvement and 34% for novice and lower-skilled workers; supports experience-curve compression and heterogeneous complementarity rather than universal replacement.

title: AI tutoring outperforms in-class active learning: an RCT introducing a novel research-based design in an authentic educational setting
book_use: Chapter 12: randomized trial with 194 Harvard undergraduate physics students found a carefully designed AI tutor produced greater learning in less time than the comparison active-learning class; supports the possibility of pedagogically designed augmentation.

title: Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning: Evidence from high school mathematics
book_use: Chapter 12: generative-AI assistance improved practice performance but an insufficiently constrained system could reduce subsequent unaided performance; teacher-designed hint guardrails mitigated the effect. Supports the distinction between output assistance and durable skill acquisition.

author_or_institution: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
title: OECD Digital Education Outlook 2026: Exploring Effective Uses of Generative AI in Education
book_use: Chapter 12: synthesizes evidence on GenAI for personalized instruction, feedback, skill development and assessment while emphasizing pedagogically grounded use that strengthens rather than substitutes for human learning.

title: An instantaneous voice-synthesis neuroprosthesis
book_use: Chapter 13: intracortical BCI decoded attempted speech from 256 implanted microelectrodes in a man with ALS into instantaneous synthesized voice with paralinguistic modulation; evidence for restoration at an intimate brain-machine interface, not near-term elective enhancement.

author_or_institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology
title: Reducing Risks Posed by Synthetic Content: An Overview of Technical Approaches to Digital Content Transparency
book_use: Chapter 14: frames synthetic-content risk mitigation as a portfolio including authentication and provenance, watermarking, detection, labeling, testing and auditing; supports layered transparency rather than a single perfect detector. Final report published 2024 and NIST page updated 2026.

author_or_institution: Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity
title: C2PA Specifications 2.4
book_use: Chapter 14: current C2PA standard for certifying source and history of media through Content Credentials. Use as evidence that provenance infrastructure exists; do not equate valid provenance with truth or universal adoption.

author_or_institution: Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity
title: Human and Organizational Identity Recommendation
book_use: Chapter 14: distinguishes machine claim-signing from human or organizational provenance and recommends identity profiles for actors behind Content Credentials; supports the chapter's layered identity and authorization model.

author_or_institution: Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence
title: 2026 AI Index Report — Research and Development
book_use: Chapter 15: global AI compute capacity estimated to have grown 3.3x annually since 2022 to 17.1 million H100-equivalents; U.S. data-center concentration and leading-chip foundry concentration illustrate capital-intensive complements beneath broadly diffusing model capability.

title: Gen AI, occupational segregation and gender equality in the world of work
book_use: Chapter 15: female-dominated occupations almost twice as likely to be exposed to GenAI as male-dominated occupations, 29% versus 16%, while women remain underrepresented in AI-related jobs; evidence that new technology interacts with pre-existing occupational structure rather than beginning from a neutral labor map.

author_or_institution: Eleanor W. Dillon / Sonia Jaffe / Nicole Immorlica / Christopher T. Stanton
title: Shifting Work Patterns with Generative AI
book_use: Chapter 16: randomized six-month field experiment across 66 firms and 7,137 knowledge workers; treated users saved about two hours per week on email and reduced after-hours work, but researchers detected no shift in task quantity or composition from individual-level AI provision. Strong counterevidence to automatic organizational redesign; disclose Microsoft involvement noted by authors.
